text:
emma: heads-up: nightly docs linkcheck failed after the heading-normalize migration. Two main failures: duplicate anchors (numbered headings like `1. Overview` creating identical slugs) and a few remote images returning 404 which our new checker treats as errors.

docs-bot: CI: docs/nightly #2337 failed at linkcheck 12 logs: https://ci.example.com/builds/2337/logs

raj: can you paste the error lines? guessing the slug collisions come from list-numbered headings and nested sections.

emma: snippet: ```
ERROR linkcheck: anchors: docs/guides/scale.md: anchor collision: '#1-overview' already defined
ERROR linkcheck: remote image broken: docs/guides/ops.md: https://old-cdn.example.com/ops-diagram.png (HTTP 404)
```

olivia: for slugs i'd prefer adding explicit ids rather than changing visible text. e.g. `### 1. Overview {#1-overview-scale}`. small PRs per file are easiest to review.

raj: agreed. i'll prototype a small script to scan for duplicate slugs and output suggestions. can make `yarn docs:scan-slugs --preview`. it will not modify files unless `--apply` is passed.

olivia: i'll handle the image fixes: move canonical diagrams into `docs/assets/` and update links + alt text. small atomic PR.

docs-bot: PR #840 opened by olivia: move ops diagrams to docs/assets and add alt text.

ci-bot: PR #840 checks started.

raj: opened PR #841 with slug scanner and a README for reviewers. includes a sample suggested change output.

emma: one policy: when adding `{#...}` suffixes, keep the original slug prefix and add a short suffix (`-scale`, `-ops`) so existing links to `#1-overview` don't silently break. if necessary add redirect entries in `docs/redirects.json` for high-traffic pages.

olivia: merging #840 after CI clears.

raj: will iterate on the scanner to surface numbered-heading collisions inside admonitions and captions too. plan to add the scanner to docs CI as a pre-merge check after we validate it.

emma: thanks all. if CI still fails after these land, let's pair for 15 to inspect the full linkcheck stack. :thumbsup:
